explanation:
Please do not take this book out of the library.

---

- **持ち出す（もちだす）** — 他動詞: to take out, to bring out. Compound of 持つ（もつ）+ directional 出す. [JLPT N2]
- **〜ないでください** — negative request: "please do not." [JLPT N5]

Drive out a bug that got inside.

---

- **追い出す（おいだす）** — 他動詞: to drive out, to expel. 追う（おう, 他動詞; counterpart 自動詞 追われる）+ 出す. [JLPT N2]
- **入ってくる** — 〜てくる: directional verb indicating movement toward the speaker. "come in." [JLPT N4]

When the child comes home from school, they throw down their bag and go out to play.

---

- **放り出す（ほうりだす）** — 他動詞: to throw out, to fling out. 放る（ほうる, 他動詞; no common counterpart）+ 出す. Implies careless or forceful tossing. [JLPT N2]
- **〜て遊びに行く** — 〜ていく/くる with purpose verb: "go do X." [JLPT N4]

"Does this library also lend magazines?"

---

- **貸し出す（しだす）** — 他動詞: to lend out, to issue (books/materials). 貸す（かす, 他動詞; counterpart 借りる）+ 出す. The nominalized form 貸し出し is commonly used for library/circulation services. [JLPT N2]
- **〜していますか** — progressive/state question: in service contexts, indicates an ongoing service offering. [JLPT N4]

Extract information from the other person.

---

- **聞き出す（ききだす）** — 他動詞: to draw out (information by questioning), to elicit. 聞く（きく, 他動詞; counterpart 聞こえる）+ 出す. The 出す implies drawing something hidden to the surface. [JLPT N2]
- **相手（あいて）** — noun: the other party, counterpart. [JLPT N3]

Forcibly taking along my reluctant daughter, I went to the hospital.

---

- **連れ出す（つれだす）** — 他動詞: to take someone out (by leading them). 連れる（つれる, 他動詞; no direct counterpart; 連れる implies accompaniment）+ 出す. [JLPT N2]
- **嫌がる（いやがる）** — 他動詞: to show dislike, to be unwilling. Derived from 嫌だ（いやだ）. [JLPT N3]
- **むりやり** — adverb: forcibly, by force. [JLPT N2]

I pulled out an old photo album from the back of the closet.

---

- **引っ張り出す（ひっぱりだす）** — 他動詞: to pull out (something stored away), to drag out. 引っ張る（ひっぱる, 他動詞; no common counterpart）+ 出す. Conveys effort in extracting something from a deep or hidden place. [JLPT N2]
- **押し入れ（おしいれ）** — noun: Japanese-style built-in closet for futons and storage. [JLPT N2]
- **奥（おく）** — noun: the back, inner part, depths. [JLPT N3]

Escape from a burning house.

---

- **逃げ出す（にげだす）** — 自動詞: to run away, to flee. 逃げる（にげる, 自動詞; counterpart 逃がす（のがす）他動詞）+ 出す. The 出す emphasizes the sudden onset of the action. [JLPT N2]
- **燃えている（もえている）** — 燃える（もえる, 自動詞; counterpart 燃やす（もやす）他動詞）: to be burning. [JLPT N3]

When I opened the box, a frog jumped out.

---

- **飛び出す（とびだす）** — 自動詞/他動詞: to jump out, to dash out (自動詞); to expel (他動詞). 飛ぶ（とぶ, 自動詞; no direct counterpart）+ 出す. In this sentence used as 自動詞 with sudden action nuance. [JLPT N2]

I found the book I had been looking for on the library shelves.

---

- **見つけ出す（みつけだす）** — 他動詞: to find, to track down (something hard to locate). 見つける（みつける, 他動詞; counterpart 見つかる）+ 出す. The 出す adds the nuance of successfully locating something after effort. [JLPT N2]
- **本棚（ほんだな）** — noun: bookshelf. [JLPT N3]
- **探していた（さがしていた）** — 探す（さがす, 他動詞; counterpart 見つかる）: to search for. Past progressive indicating an ongoing prior search. [JLPT N4]

I found my missing pet.

---

- **探し出す（さがしだす）** — 他動詞: to find after searching, to track down. 探す（さがす, 他動詞; counterpart 見つかる）+ 出す. Similar to 見つけ出す but emphasizes the search process rather than the discovery moment. [JLPT N2]
- **行方不明（ゆくえふめい）** — noun/adjectival noun: missing (person/animal), whereabouts unknown. Kango compound. [JLPT N2]

I wrote down today's schedule in my notebook.

---

- **書き出す（きだす）** — 他動詞: to write down, to list out. 書く（かく, 他動詞; counterpart 書かれる）+ 出す. The 出す implies setting something out in written form for reference. [JLPT N2]
- **予定（よてい）** — noun: schedule, plan. Kango. [JLPT N4]

Dive/jump into the pool.

---

- **飛び込む（とびこむ）** — 自動詞: to jump into, to dive into, to plunge into. 飛ぶ（とぶ, 自動詞; no direct counterpart）+ 込む（こむ）. The 込む indicates entering deeply into a space. Also used figuratively for joining an organization or situation suddenly. [JLPT N2]

I rushed into the classroom in a great hurry.

---

- **駆け込む（けこむ）** — 自動詞: to run into, to dash into (seeking shelter or refuge). 駆ける（かける, 自動詞; no common counterpart）+ 込む. The 込む implies entering for a purpose — often safety, help, or refuge. [JLPT N2]
- **大急ぎ（おおいそぎ）** — adverb/noun: in a great hurry, with all possible speed. [JLPT N2]

Cut in line.

---

- **割り込む（わりこむ）** — 自動詞: to cut in, to interrupt, to butt in. 割る（わる, 他動詞; counterpart 割れる）+ 込む. Originally "split into" a space; extended to interrupting conversations or queue-jumping. [JLPT N2]
- **列（れつ）** — noun: line, queue. [JLPT N3]

Sunlight is streaming into the room, filling it.

---

- **差し込む（さしこむ）** — 自動詞: to shine in, to stream in (of light). 差す（さす, 自動詞/他動詞; 日が差す "the sun shines"）+ 込む. The 込む conveys light penetrating into an interior space. [JLPT N2]
- **日の光（ひのひかり）** — noun: sunlight. Wago phrasing. [JLPT N2]

Rain soaks into the soil.

---

- **染み込む（しみこむ）** — 自動詞: to soak in, to permeate, to be absorbed. 染みる（しみる, 自動詞; no direct counterpart）+ 込む. The 込む indicates deep penetration into a material. Also used figuratively for ideas or feelings sinking in. [JLPT N2]
- **土（つち）** — noun: soil, earth. [JLPT N3]

After showing the guest to the reception room, the secretary withdrew to the back.

---

- **引っ込む（ひっこむ）** — 自動詞: to withdraw, to retreat, to go into hiding. 引っ張る relation + 込む; originally "pull back into." Implies moving out of sight or from public view. [JLPT N2]
- **応接室（おうせつしつ）** — noun: reception room. Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **通す（とおす）** — 他動詞: to show someone in, to guide through. Counterpart 通る（とおる）自動詞. [JLPT N3]

Pack things tightly into a bag.

---

- **詰め込む（つめこむ）** — 他動詞: to pack tightly, to cram in. 詰める（つめる, 他動詞; counterpart 詰む（つむ））+ 込む. The 込む emphasizes filling to capacity. [JLPT N2]

Swallow food without chewing.

---

- **飲み込む（のみこむ）** — 他動詞: to swallow, to gulp down. 飲む（のむ, 他動詞; no direct counterpart）+ 込む. Also used figuratively: 意味を飲み込む "grasp the meaning." [JLPT N2]
- **かまずに** — かむ（噛む, 他動詞: to chew）+ ずに: without doing. [JLPT N3]

Carry moving boxes into the room.

---

- **運び込む（はこびこむ）** — 他動詞: to carry in, to bring in (by transporting). 運ぶ（はこぶ, 他動詞; counterpart 運ばれる）+ 込む. [JLPT N2]
- **引っ越し（ひっこし）** — noun: moving (residence). 引っ越す（ひっこす, 自動詞）nominalized. [JLPT N3]

Enter data into a computer.

---

- **打ち込む（うちこむ）** — 他動詞: to type in, to input (data); also "to devote oneself to." 打つ（うつ, 他動詞; no direct counterpart）+ 込む. In computing context, refers to keyboard input. The "devote oneself" sense comes from the idea of immersing oneself deeply. [JLPT N2]
- **データ** — noun: data. [JLPT N3]

Pour love into one's child.

---

- **注ぎ込む（そそぎこむ）** — 他動詞: to pour into, to invest (time, effort, love). 注ぐ（そそぐ, 他動詞; counterpart also as 自動詞 "flow"）+ 込む. The 込む adds intensity — pouring deeply or completely. Used both literally (liquid) and figuratively (emotions, effort). [JLPT N2]
- **愛情（あいじょう）** — noun: affection, love. Kango. [JLPT N3]

Lead a friend down the path of evil.

---

- **引き込む（ひきこむ）** — 他動詞: to pull into, to drag into (a situation), to entice. 引く（ひく, 他動詞; counterpart 引かれる）+ 込む. Negative connotation — pulling someone into something undesirable. [JLPT N2]
- **悪の道（あくのみち）** — noun: the path of evil/wrongdoing. Literary phrasing. [JLPT N2]

Write comments/notes in a notebook.

---

- **書き込む（きこむ）** — 他動詞: to write in, to fill in (a form, notebook, etc.). 書く（かく, 他動詞; counterpart 書かれる）+ 込む. The 込む implies writing into a bounded space or filling in details. [JLPT N2]
- **感想（かんそう）** — noun: impression,感想. Kango. [JLPT N3]

I got caught up in the accident and was injured.

---

- **巻き込む（まきこむ）** — 他動詞: to drag into, to involve, to entangle. 巻く（まく, 他動詞; counterpart 巻かれる）+ 込む. The 込む indicates pulling someone deeply into a situation. Often used in passive form 巻き込まれる as here. [JLPT N2]
- **事故（じこ）** — noun: accident. Kango. [JLPT N4]
- **けがをした** — けがをする: to get injured. [JLPT N4]

Drive a flock of sheep into a pen.

---

- **追い込む（おいこむ）** — 他動詞: to drive into, to corner, to push into a difficult situation. 追う（おう, 他動詞; counterpart 追われる）+ 込む. Literal sense: herding animals. Figurative: cornering someone (psychologically, financially). [JLPT N2]
- **囲い（かこい）** — noun: enclosure, pen, fence. 囲う（かこう, 他動詞）nominalized. [JLPT N2]

In some countries, red is said to be a color that brings in good luck.

---

- **呼び込む（よびこむ）** — 他動詞: to invite in, to attract, to bring in. 呼ぶ（よぶ, 他動詞; counterpart 呼ばれる）+ 込む. Figurative sense: attracting fortune, customers, etc. [JLPT N2]
- **運（うん）** — noun: luck, fortune. [JLPT N3]
- **〜と言われている** — passive + ている: "it is said that." Common reporting structure. [JLPT N3]

Slump down into a chair from exhaustion.

---

- **座り込む（すわりこむ）** — 自動詞: to sit down heavily, to plop down (and stay). 座る（すわる, 自動詞; no common counterpart）+ 込む. The 込む adds the nuance of settling in deeply or staying put. [JLPT N2]

I was bedridden for a week due to illness.

---

- **寝込む（ねこむ）** — 自動詞: to be bedridden, to be laid up (with illness). 寝る（ねる, 自動詞; no counterpart）+ 込む. The 込む implies being stuck in bed, unable to get up. Always associated with illness or injury. [JLPT N2]

I talked on the phone with a friend for three hours straight.

---

- **話し込む（はなしこむ）** — 自動詞: to get absorbed in conversation, to talk deeply/earnestly. 話す（はなす, 他動詞; counterpart 話される）+ 込む. The 込む indicates becoming engrossed or deeply engaged. [JLPT N2]

My mother falls silent when she is in a bad mood.

---

- **黙り込む（だまりこむ）** — 自動詞: to fall silent, to become mute (suddenly). 黙る（だまる, 自動詞; no common counterpart）+ 込む. The 込む emphasizes the sudden or complete nature of the silence. [JLPT N2]
- **不機嫌（ふきげん）** — na-adjective/noun: in a bad mood, sulky. Kango. [JLPT N2]

Stay at the hospital around the clock to care for someone.

---

- **泊まり込む（とまりこむ）** — 自動詞: to stay overnight (at a place), to lodge continuously. 泊まる（とまる, 自動詞; counterpart 泊める（とめる）他動詞）+ 込む. The 込む implies staying continuously rather than just one night. [JLPT N2]
- **看病する（かんびょうする）** — verb: to nurse, to care for a sick person. Kango + する. [JLPT N2]

Become a disciple and live at the master's house.

---

- **住み込む（すみこむ）** — 自動詞: to live in (as a resident employee/live-in worker). 住む（すむ, 自動詞; no common counterpart）+ 込む. The 込む implies residing as part of one's work or role, not just living somewhere. [JLPT N2]
- **弟子（でし）** — noun: disciple, apprentice. [JLPT N2]
- **師匠（ししょう）** — noun: master, teacher (of a traditional art or craft). [JLPT N2]

Simmer on low heat.

---

- **煮込む（にこむ）** — 他動詞: to simmer, to stew (for a long time). 煮る（にる, 他動詞; no common counterpart）+ 込む. The 込む indicates cooking thoroughly over an extended period. [JLPT N2]
- **弱火（よわび）** — noun: low heat, gentle fire. [JLPT N2]

Push/sell a new product (aggressively).

---

- **売り込む（うりこむ）** — 他動詞: to promote, to push sales of, to pitch. 売る（うる, 他動詞; counterpart 売れる）+ 込む. The 込む conveys aggressive or earnest effort in selling/promoting. Also used for self-promotion (自分を売り込む). [JLPT N2]
- **新製品（しんせいひん）** — noun: new product. Kango. [JLPT N2]

Bowing my head, I earnestly begged my senior.

---

- **頼み込む（たのみこむ）** — 他動詞: to beg earnestly, to plead, to request persistently. 頼む（たのむ, 他動詞; counterpart 頼まれる）+ 込む. The 込む adds intensity and persistence to the request. [JLPT N2]
- **頭を下げる（あたまをさげる）** — phrase: to bow one's head; to show humility or apologize. [JLPT N2]
- **先輩（せんぱい）** — noun: senior (in school, workplace). Kango. [JLPT N3]

I patiently taught the animal tricks through repetition.

---

- **教え込む（おしえこむ）** — 他動詞: to drill into, to teach thoroughly (by repetition), to instill. 教える（おしえる, 他動詞; counterpart 教わる）+ 込む. The 込む implies repeated, intensive teaching until it becomes ingrained. [JLPT N2]
- **根気よく（こんきよく）** — adverb: patiently, with perseverance. [JLPT N2]
- **芸（げい）** — noun: trick, skill (especially of animals or performers). [JLPT N2]

"Violence is not the answer. Let's talk it over and resolve this."

---

- **話し合う（はなしあう）** — 他動詞/自動詞: to discuss, to talk things over. 話す（はなす, 他動詞; counterpart 話される）+ 合う（あう）. The 合う indicates mutual/reciprocal action — both parties participate in the discussion. [JLPT N2]
- **暴力（ぼうりょく）** — noun: violence. Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **解決する（かいけつする）** — verb: to resolve, to solve. Kango + する. [JLPT N3]

We each said what we wanted to say, and in the end we made up.

---

- **言い合う（いいあう）** — 他動詞: to say to each other, to argue, to exchange words. 言う（いう, 他動詞; counterpart 言われる）+ 合う. Can mean either friendly exchange or heated argument depending on context. [JLPT N2]
- **言いたいこと** — 言いたい (want to say) + こと: "things one wants to say." [JLPT N4]
- **仲直りした（なかなおりした）** — 仲直りする（なかなおりする）: to make up, to reconcile. [JLPT N2]

I talked deeply with a friend I hadn't seen in a while until late at night.

---

- **語り合う（たりあう）** — 他動詞: to talk earnestly with each other, to have a heartfelt conversation. 語る（かたる, 他動詞; counterpart 語られる）+ 合う. 語る is more literary/emotional than 話す, implying deeper, more meaningful conversation. [JLPT N2]

The two of them gazed into each other's eyes.

---

- **見つめ合う（みつめあう）** — 他動詞: to gaze at each other, to look deeply into each other. 見つめる（みつめる, 他動詞; no common counterpart）+ 合う. The 合う marks the reciprocal nature — mutual gazing. [JLPT N2]
- **互いの目（たがいのめ）** — 互い（たがい）: each other, mutual. [JLPT N2]

Sit facing the other person.

---

- **向かい合う（むかいあう）** — 自動詞: to face each other, to be opposite. 向かう（むかう, 自動詞; no common counterpart）+ 合う. The 合う indicates mutual positioning — face-to-face. Also used figuratively for confronting issues. [JLPT N2]

"Let's help each other when someone is in trouble."

---

- **助け合う（たすけあう）** — 他動詞: to help each other, to assist mutually. 助ける（たすける, 他動詞; counterpart 助けられる/助かる）+ 合う. The 合う marks reciprocal action. [JLPT N2]
- **困ったとき（こまったとき）** — 困る（こまる, 自動詞: to be in trouble）+ とき: "when (someone) is in trouble." [JLPT N4]

We all shared one piece of bread and ate it.

---

- **分け合う（わけあう）** — 他動詞: to share, to divide and share among themselves. 分ける（わける, 他動詞; counterpart 分かれる）+ 合う. The 合う implies sharing among multiple people. [JLPT N2]

The siblings pooled their money together and bought a gift for their parents.

---

- **出し合う（だしあう）** — 他動詞: to pool together, to contribute jointly. 出す（だす, 他動詞; counterpart 出される）+ 合う. The 合う indicates each person contributing their share toward a common purpose. [JLPT N2]
- **プレゼント** — noun: present, gift. [JLPT N4]

We agreed not to disclose the meeting contents to outsiders.

---

- **申し合わせる（もうしあわせる）** — 他動詞: to agree upon, to arrange beforehand, to come to a mutual understanding. 申す（もうす, 謙譲語 of 言う）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる implies coordinating positions. Formal/written register due to 申す. [JLPT N2]
- **会議（かいぎ）** — noun: meeting, conference. Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **外部（がいぶ）** — noun: outside, exterior, external parties. Kango. [JLPT N2]

We classmates invited each other and went to Mt. Fuji together.

---

- **誘い合わせる（さそいあわせる）** — 他動詞: to invite each other, to organize together by mutual invitation. 誘う（さそう, 他動詞; counterpart 誘われる）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる adds the nuance of coordinating invitations among a group. [JLPT N2]
- **クラスメート** — noun: classmate. [JLPT N3]

I became friends with someone I happened to sit next to on the shinkansen.

---

- **隣り合わせる（となりあわせる）** — 自動詞: to happen to be next to, to be seated beside (by chance). 隣（となり）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる implies an incidental alignment of positions. Key nuance: chance/accidental proximity, not deliberate seating. [JLPT N2]
- **新幹線（しんかんせん）** — noun: bullet train, shinkansen. [JLPT N3]
- **たまたま** — adverb: by chance, accidentally, coincidentally. [JLPT N2]

Assemble parts to make a plastic model.

---

- **組み合わせる（くみあわせる）** — 他動詞: to combine, to put together, to assemble. 組む（くむ, 他動詞; counterpart 組まれる）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる indicates matching and fitting components together. [JLPT N2]
- **部品（ぶひん）** — noun: parts, components. Kango. [JLPT N2]
- **プラモデル** — noun: plastic model kit. [JLPT N2]

Various sweets are packed together in one box.

---

- **詰め合わせる（つめあわせる）** — 他動詞: to pack an assortment, to arrange a mixed selection. 詰める（つめる, 他動詞; counterpart 詰む（つむ））+ 合わせる. The 合わせる implies arranging different items together in a set — commonly used for gift boxes (菓子詰め合わせ). [JLPT N2]
- **お菓子（おかし）** — noun: sweets, confectionery, snacks. [JLPT N3]

When I overlaid and considered the two incidents together, commonalities emerged.

---

- **重ね合わせる（さねあわせる）** — 他動詞: to overlap, to layer; figuratively to compare/overlay (events, situations). 重ねる（かさねる, 他動詞; counterpart 重ねられる）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる implies placing two things side by side for comparison. [JLPT N2]
- **事件（じけん）** — noun: incident, case, event (often criminal). Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **浮かび上がった（うかびあがった）** — 浮かび上がる（うかびあがる, 自動詞: to come to the surface, to emerge): past tense. [JLPT N2]

The culprit took customers who happened to be present as hostages and fled.

---

- **居合わせる（いあわせる）** — 自動詞: to happen to be present, to be on the scene (by chance). 居る（いる, 自動詞）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる indicates incidental co-presence. Key nuance: being there by chance, not by plan. [JLPT N2]
- **犯人（はんにん）** — noun: criminal, culprit. Kango. [JLPT N3]
- **人質（ひとじち）** — noun: hostage. Wago reading (contrast kango reading じんしつ in some contexts). [JLPT N2]
- **逃走した（とうそうした）** — 逃走する（とうそうする）: to flee, to escape. Kango + する. [JLPT N2]

When I was stranded on the bus without small change, someone who happened to be riding the same bus lent me 200 yen.

---

- **乗り合わせる（のりあわせる）** — 自動詞: to happen to be riding the same vehicle, to share a ride (by chance). 乗る（のる, 自動詞; no common counterpart）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる marks chance co-presence on the same transport. [JLPT N2]
- **小銭（こぜに）** — noun: small change, coins. [JLPT N2]
- **困っていたら** — 困る（こまる）+ ていたら: "if/when (I) was in trouble." Conditional. [JLPT N3]

"I'm sorry, I don't have my business card with me today."

---

- **持ち合わせる（もちあわせる）** — 他動詞: to have on one's person, to have available (usually money, items). 持つ（もつ, 他動詞; counterpart 持たれる）+ 合わせる. The 合わせる originally meant "to have at one's disposal." Often used in negative form. Note: humble/formal speech uses 持っておりませんで instead of 持っていません. [JLPT N2]
- **名刺（めいし）** — noun: business card. Kango. [JLPT N3]
